newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand drops charges against former SEC chief.
newsitem.headline: Thailand drops charges against former SEC chief.

text.p: Thailand's Attorney General on Thursday said the government had dropped charges against Ekamol Khiriwat, the former head of the Securities and Exchange Commisssion (SEC) and deputy governor of the Bank of Thailand.

Former finance minister Surakiart Sathirathai forced Ekamol to quit the SEC and dismissed him from his concurrent central bank post last December after alleging he had leaked confidential information.
But the Attorney General's office said in a statement the Ministry of Finance and other plaintiffs had failed to reveal witnesses or provide enough evidence to back up the charges.

"The Office of Attorney-General found the witnesses and evidence brought against the accused are not strong enough to file a lawsuit against him, so it decided to drop charges against Ekamol Khiriwat," said the statement.
Ekamol, who has said he would file defamation suits against Surakiart, the bank governor and national intelligence chief, was not avialble for comment.
